lesson.text: Quick memory: who built a printing press in Germany in about 1440? (Johannes Gutenberg.) Today: more inventors and engineers, and how they changed our lives.
Inventors make new things. Engineers design and build machines, bridges and buildings that work safely. Both solve problems, test their ideas and learn from what goes wrong.
In 1206, the engineer Al-Jazari wrote a book of 50 clever machines: water clocks, pumps and moving figures. In 1769, James Watt made the steam engine much better, and steam soon powered factories.
In 1800, Alessandro Volta made the first electric battery, a pile of metal discs. In 1829, George and Robert Stephenson's steam train Rocket won a famous race, and railways spread.
In 1843, Ada Lovelace wrote what many call the first computer program, for a machine that was never finished. In 1876, Alexander Graham Bell made the telephone, so voices could travel along wires.
In 1886, Karl Benz built a car with a petrol engine. In 1888 Bertha Benz drove it 106 km to show that it worked. In 1903, the Wright brothers made the first powered aeroplane flight: 12 seconds!

Inventors are all kinds of people. Margaret Knight's machine made paper bags (1871), and Josephine Cochrane made a dishwasher (1886). Mary Anderson made a windscreen wiper (1903), and Garrett Morgan a traffic signal (1923).

Try it in the world: build a museum of inventions with a timeline, from Al-Jazari's water clock to John Logie Baird's television (1926). Then sketch an invention of your own, and say what problem it solves.

exercises.hint: Think of voices travelling along wires.
exercises.explain: Alexander Graham Bell made the telephone in 1876.

exercises.prompt: The Wright brothers made the first powered aeroplane flight in 1903.
exercises.explain: True: in 1903 their aeroplane flew for 12 seconds.

choices: designs and builds machines and structures
exercises.explain: Engineers design and build machines, bridges and buildings that work safely.

exercises.hint: It helps drivers see in the rain.

exercises.prompt: Match each inventor to their invention.
exercises.hint: Think back through the lesson's years.
exercises.explain: Watt: a better steam engine. Volta: the battery. Benz: a petrol car. Morgan: a traffic signal.

exercises.prompt: Put these in time order, oldest first.
exercises.hint: Look for the years in the lesson.
exercises.explain: Al-Jazari (1206), Volta (1800), Bell (1876), then the Wright brothers' flight (1903).

exercises.prompt: The first powered flight was in 1903, and Baird showed television in 1926. How many years apart are they?
exercises.hint: Take the earlier year from the later one.

exercises.prompt: Ada Lovelace wrote a program for a computing machine in 1843.
exercises.explain: True: in 1843 she wrote what many call the first computer program.

exercises.prompt: Why did Bertha Benz drive 106 km in 1888?
exercises.hint: People did not yet believe cars were useful.
choices: to show people the car really worked
exercises.explain: To show that the car really worked, on a long journey. People then wanted to buy one.

exercises.prompt: Which of these could not have been made before Volta's battery?
exercises.explain: The telephone: it needs electricity to carry voices. The others need no electricity.

exercises.prompt: Al-Jazari wrote his book in 1206, and Watt improved the steam engine in 1769. How many years apart are they?
exercises.hint: Take the earlier year from the later one.

exercises.prompt: Inventors usually get everything right the first time.
exercises.hint: What does the design cycle say about testing?
exercises.explain: False: inventors test, find what goes wrong and improve, often many times.

exercises.prompt: Garrett Morgan's signal had a warning between stop and go. Why did that help?
exercises.hint: What happens if a signal changes suddenly?
choices: drivers had time to stop safely
exercises.explain: The warning gave drivers time to slow down and stop safely.

exercises.hint: Find each year in the lesson, then compare it with 1850.
exercises.explain: Before 1850: Watt (1769), Volta (1800), Rocket (1829). After: Bell (1876), Benz (1886), Baird (1926).

exercises.prompt: How long was the Wright brothers' first flight?
exercises.hint: It was very short, but it was a start.
exercises.explain: 12 seconds. Later that day, a flight lasted 59 seconds.
